answer: Hello! I'm CLVA, the Course Leader Virtual Assistant for BSc (Hons) Computer Science at the University of Wolverhampton. Ask me about deadlines, submissions, extensions, modules, timetables or university support.
Goodbye, and good luck with your studies!
You're welcome. Is there anything else I can help with?
Assessment dates for each module are published in the module's assessment area on Canvas (canvas.wlv.ac.uk) and in the module guide. If you are unsure of a date, ask your module leader.

Coursework is normally submitted online through the module's page on Canvas (canvas.wlv.ac.uk). Check the assessment brief and module guide for the required format, and ask your module leader if the submission point is not clear.

If you cannot meet a deadline, apply for an extension before the deadline through e:Vision. The rules on who can have an extension and for how long are in the University Academic Regulations and the Assessment Handbook. ASK@WLV can help with the request (01902 518518, or log a helpcall in e:Vision).

Work handed in after the deadline without an approved extension or extenuating circumstances claim may not be accepted or may be penalised. The exact rules are in the University Academic Regulations and the Assessment Handbook. If you have missed a deadline, contact your module leader or ASK@WLV straight away.

If illness or a serious problem affects an assessment, submit an extenuating circumstances claim in e:Vision. By sitting an exam you declare yourself fit to sit, so a claim for that exam becomes invalid once you begin. If your claim is approved but you decide to sit the exam, retract the claim in e:Vision first. Claims for personal events such as holidays or weddings are not accepted.

Academic misconduct includes plagiarism, collusion and cheating, whether deliberate or unintentional. Cases are investigated by the Conduct and Appeals Unit and penalties apply if proven. Reference your sources carefully, and for generative AI tools such as ChatGPT ask your module tutor what is allowed in each assignment. Skills for Learning in the Library has guidance on referencing and AI.

Your teaching timetable is in MyTimeTable at mytimetable.wlv.ac.uk/schedule. Log in with your University account. You can view it by day, week or month, sync it with Outlook, and it updates automatically when sessions change. It is also available through the myWLV app.

Registering your attendance is compulsory. At each timetabled session, open Student Check-In in the myWLV app or at myattendance.wlv.ac.uk, choose the session, select Present and enter the six-digit code from your lecturer. If you cannot attend, report the absence in Student Check-In. If your record looks wrong, contact ASK@WLV.

answer: For a question about one module, contact the module leader, whose details are on the module's Canvas page. For course-level questions, contact your course leader or personal tutor. ASK@WLV is the first point of contact for general student queries: log a helpcall in e:Vision, call 01902 518518, or visit the Ambika Paul Building at City Campus, Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm. You can also book a one-to-one with your Student Success Coach.

Feedback and marks for coursework are returned through the module's Canvas page, and your confirmed results are published in e:Vision after the assessment boards. If a mark is missing or looks wrong, contact your module leader or ASK@WLV.

If you do not pass an assessment you may be offered a resit. Semester one resits normally take place in the May exam period, and resits for semester two and year-long modules in July. The number of attempts allowed and how resit marks are treated are set out in the University Academic Regulations. Check e:Vision for what you need to resit.

Your personal exam timetable is published in e:Vision, usually two weeks before the exam period. Provisional exam dates are shown in the module's assessment area on Canvas. The main exam periods are in January and May, with resits in July. Bring your University ID card (or other photo ID) and your own stationery. Phones and smartwatches must be switched off and stored away. Contact exams@wlv.ac.uk with questions, or call 01902 32 2494 on the day of an exam.

Borrow and return books at the self-service kiosks in any University library using your University ID card. Undergraduates can borrow up to 30 items. Loans are for one week and renew automatically for up to a year unless someone requests the item. Fines of GBP 1 a day apply only to requested items returned late. Search for books, e-books and journals in LibrarySearch (librarysearch.wlv.ac.uk). The Library ASSIST chat service is available 24/7, or call 01902 32 1333.

answer: Contact the IT Service Desk on 01902 322000 (24 hours), email itsupport@wlv.ac.uk, use the IT Support Portal, or drop in at the Harrison Library, City Campus (Monday, Tuesday and Thursday, 9am to 4pm). To reset a forgotten password go to passwordreset.microsoftonline.com; you will need your phone for multifactor authentication. For Wi-Fi, connect to eduroam with your University email address and password; on phones and tablets use the geteduroam app.

The referencing style for your subject is stated in your module guide and on Canvas. Skills for Learning in the Library runs Harvard Referencing (Cite Them Right) workshops and offers drop-in help from librarians. The University's reference management tool is RefWorks, which is being renamed EndNote Fusion.

The Mental Health and Wellbeing team offers free, confidential support. Complete the registration form on the Student Support pages and the team will contact you within two working days (mhwenquiries@wlv.ac.uk). WLV Student Life Connect is available 24/7 on 0333 212 0672. For disability, neurodiversity or long-term health conditions, email disability-inclusion@wlv.ac.uk. For money worries, ask about the Dennis Turner Hardship Fund. The Student Life desk is in the Ambika Paul Building, City Campus, Monday to Friday 10am to 4pm. If you need urgent help, see the 'I need help now' page on the University website.

If you are thinking about changing course, changing a module, taking a leave of absence or withdrawing, talk to your course leader, personal tutor or Student Success Coach first, then contact ASK@WLV (01902 518518, or a helpcall in e:Vision), who will explain the process. The University publishes Leave of Absence Guidelines on its regulations page.
